title: BDS in China: Dentistry Universities, Fees & Entry
description: Study BDS (dentistry) in China: what the degree is called, how long it takes, entry requirements, fees and how to check it is recognised in your country.
h1: BDS in China for international students
intro: Dentistry in China is taught as a five-year bachelor's degree in stomatology (口腔医学), often written as BDS or Bachelor of Dental Surgery in English-language offers. Fewer universities teach it in English than teach MBBS, so the shortlist is shorter and the application windows matter more.

sections.h: What the degree is and how long it takes
p: Chinese universities award a Bachelor of Stomatology. The course combines basic medical science, dental science and clinical training, and most programs run five years with clinical practice built in. Some universities add a supervised internship year, so always read the program page for the exact length.

sections.h: BDS in China fee and cost
p: Tuition for BDS in China depends on the university, the city and whether the course is taught in English. Fees are set each year, so CAS keeps no fixed number on this page. Open any university in the catalog to see its current tuition, then add accommodation, medical insurance and living costs for the city you choose.
ul: Tuition: set per university and per year
Accommodation: usually a campus dormitory, priced per room type
Living costs: lower in smaller cities than in Beijing or Shanghai

sections.h: BDS in China eligibility criteria and requirements
p: Most universities ask for a completed high-school certificate with a science stream (biology and chemistry, often physics), a recent passport, a health check and a police certificate. Some ask for English proof and a short interview. Age limits and minimum grades differ by university, so check the university page before applying.

A dental degree is only useful if your home country accepts it for licensing. Dental councils and ministries change their rules and each country sets its own licensing exam. Ask your national dental council for its current list of accepted foreign dental degrees before you pay any application fee. CAS will tell you which Chinese universities teach dentistry in English, but the recognition decision is your country's.

Chinese Government (CSC), provincial and university scholarships can cover tuition and part of living costs for medical and dental programs. Awards are competitive and have their own deadlines, listed on the scholarships page.

We check your documents against the university's current rules, apply for you, help with the visa, and meet you on arrival. The free study plan tells you which universities and programs fit your grades and budget before you commit to anything.

faq.q: How many years is BDS in China?
faq.a: Most English-taught dental programs are five years, sometimes with an added internship. The exact length is on each program page.

faq.q: What are the BDS in China eligibility criteria?
faq.a: Usually a science-stream high-school certificate, a valid passport, a health check and a police certificate. Grade and age limits vary by university.

faq.q: What does BDS in China cost?
faq.a: Tuition differs by university and changes every year, so check the current figure on the university page, then add accommodation, insurance and living costs.

faq.q: Is a BDS from China valid in my country?
faq.a: That depends on your country's dental council. Confirm its current rules for foreign dental degrees before you apply.

faq.q: Can I study BDS in China in English?
faq.a: Yes, at some universities. Fewer teach dentistry in English than MBBS, so shortlist early.

answer: BDS in China is a bachelor's degree in stomatology that usually takes five years. Entry normally needs a science-stream high-school certificate, and you should confirm with your own dental council that the degree is accepted before you apply.

title: Chinese Language Program in China: Courses & Entry
description: Chinese language programs at universities in China: one-semester to one-year courses, HSK preparation, entry requirements, visas and scholarships.
h1: Chinese language program in China
intro: A Chinese language program is a non-degree course taught at a Chinese university to build speaking, listening, reading and writing. It is the usual first step for students who plan a Chinese-taught degree, and a short course for anyone who wants to live in China and learn the language.

p: Programs run from a few weeks of summer study to one semester, one academic year or two years. Intakes are typically in September and March, and some universities add short courses. The study in China for six months question usually means one semester.
Classes are graded by level and prepare for the HSK exam. Expect daily classes in grammar, reading, listening and spoken Chinese, with cultural activities on top.
Most universities need a high-school certificate, a valid passport, a health check and a police certificate. No Chinese is needed for beginner levels.
Courses longer than 180 days usually need an X1 visa, which you convert to a residence permit after arrival. Shorter courses use an X2 visa. Your admission letter states which applies.

Tuition for language courses is lower than for degrees and is set by each university. Chinese Government, provincial and university scholarships fund language study in some routes; see the scholarships page.
